overview.headline: Continuous circulation of water between Earth and atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the water cycle moves water from ground to atmosphere and back again.
keyPoints.quote: At its core, the water cycle is the motion of the water from the ground to the atmosphere and back again.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that condensation changes water vapor into liquid water.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that precipitation falls as rain, hail, snow or sleet.
keyPoints.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that runoff occurs when saturated ground cannot absorb excess precipitation.
keyPoints.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: Change of state from liquid to gas requiring energy
keyTerms.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyTerms.gloss: Evaporation of water from plants through leaf openings
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: Process where water vapor changes into liquid water
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: Fresh water falling as rain, hail, snow or sleet
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: Results of excess water forming rivers and lakes
keyTerms.quote: Rivers and lakes are results of runoff.

keyTerms.gloss: Condition when air temperature equals dew point and fog forms
keyTerms.quote: Foggy conditions often occur when air temperature and dew point are equal.
